solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With revision, Fine Art & Lit gradually sink in

indicators.note: a revision reworks a text, so these letters are recast in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An art student, revising Fine Art and Literature, hopes the material will slowly soak in.
explanation.walkthrough: The ampersand is only a joining link; the letters of FINE ART and LIT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To infiltrate is to permeate or seep into something little by little, a synonym for gradually sinking in.

clue.text: Independence: it hurt one US state

parts.note: I is an abbreviation for independent or independence
ow is the cry when something hurts
a means one, as in a dollar

explanation.surface: Gaining independence was a painful process for one American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a state of the American Midwest.

clue.text: Perhaps failed to catch Facebook exchange to bottom left

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the social network is swapped in where the rear's opening letter stood, wrapping what remains
the opening letter of the rear is given up to make way for the social network's letters

parts.note: bum is British slang for the backside
led as in led the way, departed first

explanation.surface: Someone's social-media swapping goes so badly it leaves them on their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange to' swaps the B of the backside for Facebook's two letters, which wrap round the UM left behind; departed then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder who fumbles has mishandled the ball, one example of failing to take a catch, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Agitating, in sum, actually causes bedlam

indicators.note: agitating means stirring up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stirring up trouble, in short, actually creates chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam was the London hospital for the insane, so its name came to mean a madhouse.

clue.text: What Martinez or Ferguson have bottled is put back on ice again!

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting back means the hidden letters are read in reverse
letters bottled up inside the two names are concealed within them

explanation.surface: Football managers Roberto Martinez and Alex Ferguson are said to have kept something in the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottled' hints at a manager losing his nerve, but it marks the hidden letters. NEZORFER spans Martinez and Ferguson.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has been frozen a second time is back on ice.

clue.text: Revolting man's time winding up bank

indicators.note: in a down clue, winding up means reading bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A disgusting fellow's time is up at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgusting but means rebelling: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler was the leader of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt, a famous rebel.

clue.text: The ultimate in class combined with the worst kind of people

indicators.note: the ultimate is the final item, so only the closing letter of class is taken

parts.note: cum is the Latin-derived word for together with, as in a bedroom-cum-office

explanation.surface: A snob's remark that the very best breeding is mixed in with the lowest sort of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a contemptuous term for the lowest, most worthless people, the dregs of society.

clue.text: Worked in kitchen — as did Ramsay, unhappy after brief check?

indicators.note: the swearing comes after the short form of check

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
the chef Gordon Ramsay is famous for swearing, effing and blinding when displeased

explanation.surface: Gordon Ramsay, cooking, swore when unhappy after a quick inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Ramsay is a British TV chef known for foul-mouthed outbursts; to eff is to swear.
explanation.definitionFit: To chef is to work as a cook in a professional kitchen.

clue.text: Spymaster favours melody that could 21

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
someone who favours a policy is for it
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A spy chief prefers a particular tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is SPELL DISASTER: this answer is a word that would spell disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortune is bad luck, an unlucky event, which could well bring about catastrophe.

clue.text: Greendale's Mrs Goggins, or Bloomsbury's Mrs Woolf?

definitions.meaning: Mrs Goggins runs the post office in Greendale in the children's TV series Postman Pat, so she deals in mail
Virginia Woolf of the Bloomsbury Group was a novelist and essayist, a literary figure

explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV show set in the village of Greendale, where Mrs Goggins is the postmistress. Virginia Woolf belonged to the Bloomsbury Group of London writers and artists.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is read once as a woman who handles post and once as a female writer, the postmistress and the novelist.

clue.text: See 9
Cheers! Couple will upstage one in third best fashion

indicators.note: to upstage is to push aside and take the place of, so the one is replaced

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
to cheer someone is to elate them
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A toast, after which a duo will outshine one performer in third place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers!' looks like a toast but is the verb, giving ELATES, which goes with TWO in place of I.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes the most up-to-date style or development, the height of current fashion.

clue.text: Refuse resolutely, then force and energy act unconditionally

indicators.note: read as re-fuse, melting and fusing again, so the following word is recast in new order

parts.note: taken as written
F is the physics symbol for force
go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly says no, then pushes hard and acts without any conditions attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb meaning decline, but it is the anagram signal, read as fuse again.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon restraint is to behave without holding back, without limits or conditions on oneself.

clue.text: Abusing her? Mrs Tutu means to get whoppers out

indicators.note: abusing means misusing or mistreating, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about mistreating Mrs Tutu as a way of extracting big lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whoppers' are big lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug supposed to make someone tell no lies is a means of getting lies out of them.

clue.text: Relapsing, what in the end rogue breaking in does to get censored

indicators.note: lapsing back, so the whole assembly is read in the opposite direction
the rogue and the letter before it force their way into the middle of the animals

parts.note: female deer are does, so the word stands for deer

indicators.note: points to the closing letter of what

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue

explanation.surface: A burglar relapses into crime, and what he does on breaking in gets hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe. 'breaking in' builds DETCADER, which 'Relapsing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A redacted document has had sensitive passages blacked out, which is a form of censorship.

clue.text: Together they could make you a little crook

parts.words: Together they could make you a little
parts.note: split the answer into its parts, a letter, a conjunction and a pronoun: the letter joined to the pronoun gives a word for a small amount

explanation.surface: A crook is advised that teaming up could make a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as B AND IT: B and IT together make BIT, a little.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw or robber, especially an armed one, is a crook, a criminal.

clue.text: A strike in business centre could 21

indicators.note: the article and the blow sit inside the financial district

parts.note: the City is London's financial district
to lam is to beat or hit

explanation.surface: A strike in the financial district could be a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the financial district of London. 21 is SPELL DISASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a disaster, so the word itself is a way of saying catastrophe.

clue.text: It's pity that saved one swimming pool worker

indicators.note: letters swimming about are jumbled into a new order
saved is used in its sense of except, so the one is left out

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lament that someone who rescued another got into difficulties at the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saved' means except here: ITSPITY without I leaves TSPITY, which 'swimming' rearranges. 'pool' suggests swimming but means a typing pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A typing pool was an office team of typists, so one of its staff is a pool worker.

clue.text: Bishops yet to be upbraided?

parts.note: pre- means before, so something yet to be is pre-
read as braided up, decorated with braid, like lace

explanation.surface: Bishops who have not yet been scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbraided' looks like scolded, but is read as braided up, giving LACY.
explanation.definitionFit: The prelacy is the body of prelates, high-ranking clergy such as bishops collectively.

clue.text: One fixes plateful in Barkin' greasy spoon?

parts.note: a frying pan is the greasy utensil of a cheap cafe

indicators.note: the East London speech of Barking drops initial H and final G, as the clue's own spelling of the town shows

parts.note: a helping is a plateful of food

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a plateful at a greasy-spoon cafe in Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of East London; 'in Barkin'' asks for the local pronunciation, which drops H and G from HELPING to leave ELPIN. A greasy spoon is a cheap fry-up cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel pin is a small thin nail used to fasten panels, so it is something that fixes.

clue.text: A number of columns sensationalised police court overlooking new clue

indicators.note: a story sensationalised is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
overlooking means leaving aside, and new signals the letters of the next word in any order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid sensationalised a police court case and ignored a fresh clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing C, L, U and E from POLICE COURT leaves POIORCT, which rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch with a roof held up by a row of columns.

clue.text: Foully 1ac 26ac with 6ac? That could do it for 8 and 16

definitions.meaning: to foully infiltrate mayonnaise with scum would ruin the dish, a recipe for ruin

definitions.text: That could do it for 8 and 16
definitions.meaning: misfortune and calamity are words that both mean the same as disaster

explanation.walkthrough: The first half builds a kitchen scene from three other answers: INFILTRATE, MAYO and SCUM. The second reads the phrase as giving the meaning of two other answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Contaminating food with filth would bode ruin, and misfortune and calamity each mean catastrophe, read as spelling out that word.

clue.text: Spur on back of heel that is carrying mountie over the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, this part sits above the final letter
the two letters hold the abbreviation between them

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
MP stands for Mounted Police

indicators.note: takes the last letter of heel

explanation.surface: A rider spurs on with the back of the heel, a Mountie charging over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mountie is a Canadian Mounted Policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge forward, which is what spurring on does.

clue.text: Religiously 11, as here

definitions.meaning: 11 is the latest word; the closing word of a prayer is said in agreement
the answer is the closing entry of the puzzle, the last word on the page

explanation.walkthrough: 11 down is THE LATEST WORD, read here as the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen ends prayers, the last word in religion, and this answer is the last clue in the puzzle.

clue.text: Some town-planning for which Spooner's cut the chat

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words have their first sounds exchanged

parts.note: grass that has been cut has been mowed
rap is slang for a talk or chat

explanation.surface: A puzzling account of the cutting of a chat, attributed to the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: MOWED RAP with its opening sounds swapped gives ROWED MAP, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan of streets for a town is a planning document, and a road map is one such piece of town-planning.

clue.text: The writer's composition of old is being held in great admiration

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are enclosed between the two letters for the writer is

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, so the writer is becomes I am, contracted

indicators.note: a composition puts parts together in a new arrangement, so the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author's work about the past is greatly admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer's' is the setter saying I am; 'composition of' gives DOLIS, held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolism is the worship of idols, and by extension excessive adoration or veneration of a person.

clue.text: You'll find it in the Emerald Isle dressing

definitions.text: You'll find it in the Emerald Isle
definitions.meaning: a county of western Ireland, which is called the Emerald Isle

explanation.surface: A tourist is told that a certain salad sauce is found in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emerald Isle is a poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is an Irish county, and it is also the familiar short form of mayonnaise, a dressing.

clue.text: Underestimated, at first, poison deadly bats possess

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of poison
bats is slang for crazy, so the word deadly is scrambled

parts.note: to own something is to possess it

explanation.surface: A sinister scene of bats carrying a lethal poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals but means mad, rearranging DEADLY to LAYEDD.
explanation.definitionFit: To play something down is to minimise it or treat it as less important, close to understating it.
